translation_en: Dawud ibn Rushayd narrated to us: Marwan ibn Mu‘awiyah narrated to us: ‘Umar ibn Hamzah ibn ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Umar informed us: Salim ibn ‘Abd Allah narrated to us, from his father, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Any household that keeps a dog, except a livestock dog or hunting dog, loses two qirats from its deeds every day.”

Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna and Ibn Bashshar narrated to us—and the wording is Ibn al-Muthanna’s. Muhammad ibn Ja‘far narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Qatadah, from Abu al-Hakam, who said: I heard Ibn ‘Umar narrate from the Prophet, who said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except a crop-protecting, sheep, or hunting dog, loses one qirat from his reward every day.”

Abu al-Tahir and Harmalah informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “Whoever keeps a dog that is neither a hunting dog, a livestock dog, nor a crop-protecting dog loses two qirats of his reward every day.” Abu al-Tahir’s hadith does not include “nor a crop-protecting dog.”

‘Abd ibn Humayd narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Razzaq informed us: Ma‘mar informed us, from al-Zuhri, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever keeps a dog, except a livestock, hunting, or crop-protecting dog, loses one qirat from his reward every day.” Al-Zuhri said Abu Hurayrah’s statement was mentioned to Ibn ‘Umar, who said, “May Allah have mercy on Abu Hurayrah; he owned crops.”

Zuhayr ibn Harb narrated to me: Isma‘il ibn Ibrahim narrated to us: Hisham al-Dastawa’i narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, from Abu Salamah, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever keeps a dog loses one qirat from his deeds every day, except for a crop-protecting dog or a livestock dog.”

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim informed us: Shu‘ayb ibn Ishaq narrated to us: al-Awza‘i narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to me: Abu Salamah ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman narrated to me: Abu Hurayrah narrated to me from the Messenger of Allah with a report like it.
Ahmad ibn al-Mundhir narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Samad narrated to us: Harb narrated to us: Yahya ibn Abi Kathir narrated to us, with this chain and a report like it.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahid, meaning Ibn Ziyad, narrated to us, from Isma‘il ibn Sumay‘: Abu Razin narrated to us. He said: I heard Abu Hurayrah say the Messenger of Allah said: “Whoever keeps a dog that is neither a hunting dog nor a sheepdog loses one qirat from his deeds every day.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Yazid ibn Khusayfah, that al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid informed him that he heard Sufyan ibn Abi Zuhayr, a man from Shanū’ah among the Messenger’s Companions, say: I heard the Messenger of Allah say: “Whoever keeps a dog that does not help him with crops or livestock loses one qirat from his deeds every day.” He was asked, “Did you hear this from the Messenger of Allah?” He said, “Yes, by the Lord of this mosque.”

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah, and Ibn Hujr narrated to us: Isma‘il narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Khusayfah, who informed me that al-Sa’ib ibn Yazid said Sufyan ibn Abi Zuhayr al-Shana’i visited them and reported a hadith like it from the Messenger of Allah.

Yahya ibn Ayyub, Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id, and ‘Ali ibn Hujr narrated to us: Isma‘il, meaning Ibn Ja‘far, narrated to us, from Humayd, who said: Anas ibn Malik was asked about a cupper’s earnings. He said: The Messenger of Allah was cupped by Abu Tibah. He ordered two measures of food for him and spoke to his family, who reduced his tax. He said: “The best treatment you use is cupping, or it is among your best remedies.”

Ibn Abi ‘Umar narrated to us: Marwan, al-Fazari, narrated to us, from Humayd, who said Anas was asked about a cupper’s earnings and mentioned a report like it, except that he said: “The best treatment you use is cupping and Indian costus. Do not torment your children with pressing.”

Ahmad ibn al-Hasan ibn Khirash narrated to us: Shababah narrated to us: Shu‘bah narrated to us, from Humayd, who said: I heard Anas say: The Prophet called one of our young servants who was a cupper and had him cup him. He ordered a measure, a mudd, or two mudd of food for him, and spoke on his behalf so that his tax was reduced.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Abu Kurayb narrated it to us. Abu Bakr said: Waki‘ narrated to us; Abu Kurayb—and the wording is his—said: Waki‘ informed us, from Mis‘ar, from ‘Amr ibn ‘Amir al-Ansari, who said: I heard Anas ibn Malik say: The Messenger of Allah was cupped, and he never wronged anyone regarding his wages.

‘Ubayd Allah ibn ‘Umar al-Qawariri narrated to us: ‘Abd al-A‘la ibn ‘Abd al-A‘la, Abu Hammam, narrated to us: Sa‘id al-Jurayri narrated to us, from Abu Nadhrah, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah address the people in Madinah. He said: “People, Allah is alluding to wine, and perhaps Allah will soon reveal a ruling concerning it. Whoever has any of it, let him sell it and benefit from its price.” We remained only a short while before the Prophet said: “Allah has now forbidden wine. Whoever this verse reaches while he has any of it must neither drink it nor sell it.” The people then went out with what they had of it onto the roads of Madinah and poured it away.

Suwayd ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Hafs ibn Mayyasar narrated to us, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa‘lah, a man from Egypt, that he came to ‘Abd Allah ibn ‘Abbas; and Abu al-Tahir narrated to us—and the wording is his—: Ibn Wahb informed us: Malik ibn Anas and others informed me, from Zayd ibn Aslam, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa‘lah al-Saba’i, from Egypt, that he asked Ibn ‘Abbas about grape juice. Ibn ‘Abbas said: A man gave the Messenger of Allah a waterskin of wine. The Messenger asked him, “Did you know that Allah has forbidden it?” He said, “No.” He then whispered to someone. The Messenger asked, “What did you whisper to him?” He said, “I ordered him to sell it.” The Messenger said: “The One who forbade drinking it also forbade selling it.” The man then opened the waterskin and poured out what was in it.

Abu al-Tahir informed me: Ibn Wahb informed us: Sulayman ibn Bilal informed me, from Yahya ibn Sa‘id, from ‘Abd al-Rahman ibn Wa‘lah, from Ibn ‘Abbas, from the Messenger of Allah, with a report like it.

Zuhayr ibn Harb and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us. Zuhayr said: Jarir narrated to us; Ishaq said: Jarir informed us, from Mansur, from Abu al-Duha, from Masruq, from ‘Aishah, who said: When the verses at the end of Surat al-Baqarah were revealed, the Messenger of Allah went out and recited them to the people, then forbade trading in wine.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Abu Kurayb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Kurayb’s. Ishaq said: He informed us; the other two said: Abu Mu‘awiyah narrated to us, from al-A‘mash, from Muslim, from Masruq, from ‘Aishah, who said: When the verses about usury at the end of Surat al-Baqarah were revealed, the Messenger of Allah went out to the mosque and forbade trading in wine.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from ‘Ata’ ibn Abi Rabah, from Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah, who heard the Messenger of Allah say in the year of the Conquest while in Makkah: “Allah and His Messenger have forbidden the sale of wine, carrion, pigs, and idols.” It was asked, “Messenger of Allah, what about the fat of carrion? Ships are coated with it, hides are treated with it, and people use it for lamps.” He said, “No, it is forbidden.” Then the Messenger of Allah said: “May Allah fight the Jews! When Allah forbade them the fat, they melted it, sold it, and consumed its price.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah and Ibn Numayr narrated to us: Abu Usamah narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Hamid ibn Ja‘far, from Yazid ibn Abi Habib, from ‘Ata’, from Jabir, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah in the year of the Conquest. Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: al-Dahhak, Abu ‘Asim, narrated to us, from ‘Abd al-Hamid, who narrated to me: Yazid ibn Abi Habib wrote to me that he heard Jabir ibn ‘Abd Allah say he heard the Messenger of Allah in the year of the Conquest, with a report like Layth’s.

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah, Zuhayr ibn Harb, and Ishaq ibn Ibrahim narrated to us—and the wording is Abu Bakr’s. They said: Sufyan ibn ‘Uyaynah narrated to us, from ‘Amr, from Tawus, from Ibn ‘Abbas, who said: ‘Umar heard that Samurah had sold wine and said, “May Allah fight Samurah! Did he not know that the Messenger of Allah said, ‘May Allah curse the Jews: fat was forbidden to them, so they melted it and sold it’?”
Umayyah ibn Bistam narrated to us: Yazid ibn Zuray‘ narrated to us: Rawh, Ibn al-Qasim, narrated to us, from ‘Amr ibn Dinar, with this chain and a report like it.

Ishaq ibn Ibrahim al-Hanzali informed us: Rawh ibn ‘Ubadah narrated to us: Ibn Jurayj narrated to us: Ibn Shihab informed me, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, who narrated to him from Abu Hurayrah, from the Messenger of Allah, who said: “May Allah fight the Jews! Allah forbade them fat, but they sold it and consumed its price.”

Harmalah ibn Yahya informed us: Ibn Wahb informed us: Yunus informed me, from Ibn Shihab, from Sa‘id ibn al-Musayyab, from Abu Hurayrah, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “May Allah fight the Jews! Fat was forbidden to them, but they sold it and consumed its price.”

Yahya ibn Yahya said: I recited to Malik, from Nafi‘, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not sell gold for gold except like for like, and do not give more of one amount than another. Do not sell silver for silver except like for like, and do not give more of one amount than another. Do not sell what is absent for what is present.”

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Layth narrated to us; Muhammad ibn Rumh informed us: al-Layth informed us, from Nafi‘, that a man from Banu Layth said to Ibn ‘Umar that Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri reported this from the Messenger of Allah. ‘Abd Allah and Nafi‘ went with him; Ibn Rumh’s report says Nafi‘ went with them. The man entered upon Abu Sa‘id and said, “This man told me that you report the Messenger of Allah forbade selling silver for silver except like for like, and gold for gold except like for like.” Abu Sa‘id pointed to his eyes and ears and said, “My eyes saw and my ears heard the Messenger of Allah say: ‘Do not sell gold for gold or silver for silver except like for like, equal for equal. Do not give more of one amount than another, and do not sell what is absent for what is present except hand to hand.’”

Shayban ibn Farrukh narrated to us: Jarir, Ibn Hazim, narrated to us; Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: ‘Abd al-Wahhab narrated to us: I heard Yahya ibn Sa‘id; and Muhammad ibn al-Muthanna narrated to us: Ibn Abi ‘Adi narrated to us, from Ibn ‘Awn. All reported from Nafi‘ with a report like Layth’s from Nafi‘, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, from the Prophet.

Qutaybah ibn Sa‘id narrated to us: Ya‘qub, Ibn ‘Abd al-Rahman al-Qari, narrated to us, from Suhayl, from his father, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, that the Messenger of Allah said: “Do not sell gold for gold or silver for silver except weight for weight, like for like, equal for equal.”

Abu Bakr ibn Abi Shaybah narrated to us: Waki‘ narrated to us: Isma‘il ibn Muslim al-‘Abdi narrated to us: Abu al-Mutawakkil al-Naji narrated to us, from Abu Sa‘id al-Khudri, who said the Messenger of Allah said: “Gold for gold, silver for silver, wheat for wheat, barley for barley, dates for dates, and salt for salt, like for like, hand to hand. Whoever gives more or asks for more has engaged in usury; the taker and giver are alike.”
